:::{#exm-lik-obs}
#### Likelihood of one Bernoulli observation

If $X \sim \Ber(\pi)$, then $\p_{\pi}(X = x) = \pi^x (1 - \pi)^{1 - x}$
for $x \in \cb{0, 1}$.
If we observe $x = 1$, the likelihood is $\Lik(\pi) = \pi$:
for example, $\Lik(0.2) = 0.2$ and $\Lik(0.7) = 0.7$,
so the observation $x = 1$ is more likely under $\pi = 0.7$
than under $\pi = 0.2$.
:::
